newsitem.title: USA: Komag sees further yield gains in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Komag sees further yield gains in Q2.

text.p: Komag Inc said product yields improved throughout the first quarter and expects to achieve more yield gains in the second quarter.
The company said that additional yield gains are necessary to achieve its previously announced targeted gross margin range of 30 percent to 35 percent for the second half of 1997.

It said it will add two new production lines during the second quarter. While the rate of growth in unit output during the second quarter should continue at a robust pace, current strong customer demand for its products will most likely outpace expected second quarter production output, it said.

Contrary to Komag's improving outlook, product transition issues at Asahi Komag Co Ltd (AKCL), its unconsolidated Japanese joint venture, will most likely cause the venture's operating performance to decline sequentially between the first and second quarters of 1997.

Given this expectation and without the positive effect of the one-time investment gain in the first quarter, AKCL's equity contribution to Komag will be sharply lower and possibly negative in the second quarter. Improved product yields at AKCL resulted in higher first quarter sales and supported a sequential improvement in its financial results.

Additionally, AKCL realized a $5.3 million after tax gain from sale of its ownership stake in Headway Technologies Inc in the first quarter. AKCL had previously written off this entire investment, the company said. A modest improvement in operating performance, combined with the significant gain on the Headway investment, accounted for the sharp rise in AKCL's net income from $0.8 million in the fourth quarter of 1996 to $6.8 million in the first quarter of 1997.
Based on its ownership stake in AKCL, Komag recognized 50 percent of AKCL's net income as equity income from AKCL, which contributed $0.06 per share to Komag's first quarter earnings.

The company said in the second half of 1997, it will add one ND-type production line in Penang. The rate of growth in the company's unit production in the second half will depend, in large measure, on the achievement of further yield gains, the levels of equipment utilization and throughput, and the effectiveness of ND sputtering lines.

Given the timing of its planned capacity additions and expected productivity improvements, the growth rate in quarterly production output, measured on a percentage basis from the prior quarter, will slow during the second half of 1997.

Coupled with strong growth in production output during the first half of the year, its expected second half performance should result in a year-over-year growth in production output that positions the company to gain market share in 1997, the company said.

For fiscal 1997, it has planned about $290 million for capital expenditures. A major portion of this total will be used to equip two new production plants, as well as its new research and development facility.
It plans to spend about $50 million on research and development during 1997, a 70 percent increase over 1996.
